findings.check: holds at the point estimates. Eight cells have a 95% upper bound of at most 0.13; n4|pop is 0.113 with a 95% interval of 0.03 to 0.19 over 8 worlds (2 of its worlds are above 0.15), it is the largest of nine estimates, and no SE includes training-seed variance. With P0u as the null it is 0.120 +/- 0.060 (the report gives 0.120 without the SE) and n1|pop falls from 0.081 to 0.063 (P0u beats P0 there).
findings.source: r5-ladder-002:out/n*/scores.npz [t*|view|K, C, P0, P0u, D@N, Dr@N]

findings.claim: C - P0 with z over 8 worlds of 3.3 to 5.2
findings.check: the z is a cluster bootstrap over 8 worlds; as a t statistic with 7 degrees of freedom the eight non-zero gaps are 1.6 to 4.7 (p about 0.002 to 0.02 for the seven with t >= 3)

findings.claim: the number of hidden parameters makes no measurable difference; not a difficulty dial
findings.check: not established either way. The hidden sets are different worlds, and the eight n8 truths happen to sit close to the prior mean on the four parameters shared with n4 (RMS 0.39 box half-widths, none beyond 0.78, against 0.55 for the n4 truths and 0.58 expected), which makes the n8 worlds easier for a reason unrelated to the count. In the block view 1 against 4 hidden parameters does differ (sigma 0.005 against 0.018, Welch t 2.9, p 0.02, uncorrected); in the population view the design cannot see differences below about 0.07. Nested truths (the same four values with parameters 5-8 added) would separate count from draw.

findings.claim: identifiability worsens with the number of hidden parameters; passive episodes identify as well as inputs once 4 or more are hidden, so experiments are not needed
findings.check: both are statements about this scripted inference at a fixed design size, not about the world. The design has 768 points in 4 and in 8 dimensions and the posterior is floored by the emulator's misfit: for the shared parameter lR the block-view SD ratio at 512 episodes is 0.026, 0.098, 0.418 for 1, 4, 8 hidden parameters while its projection R2 falls 0.83, 0.59, 0.48, and 256 times more data moves the n8 contraction only from 0.69 to 0.51. The single-class arms have 2 design episodes per point. With 1 hidden parameter, where the floor is low, the aimed push does help (0.45-0.72 of the passive SD). What is supported: identification is not the bottleneck for these predictors (S(2) within 0.004 of C; 0.018 in the population view). Whether designed inputs carry more information at 4-8 parameters is untested.

findings.claim: with rollouts expect agents at S whatever their strength (block, object views)
findings.check: not supported. sigma and rho are relative to C, one net per view trained once for 6,000 steps (5-24 seconds; best validation at the last or second-to-last evaluation in all nine cells), which sees 5 lagged frames of the history. C is at 0.35-0.69 OES, so 0.31-0.65 of the oracle's skill is not reached, and whether a stronger history-only predictor reaches more of it was not tested. The study shows that knowing the parameters adds little for this net family; it does not show that C is the ceiling, and an agent that predicts better than C scores above S.

findings.claim: the data-only learner needs 105-451 episodes and never reaches S(2); value of theory 53-226x and more than 256x
findings.check: numbers reproduced, but D(512) is limited by its schedule in the block and object views: 47 of 48 nets have their best validation step at 2,250 or later of 2,500 (31 at the last evaluation), so N90 of D is an upper bound there and the ratios are inflated by an unknown factor. N90 is interpolated in log2 between two measured budgets a factor 4 apart. In n4|pop D(512) equals S(2) within 0.0004 OES, so 'more than 256x' is 'about 256x' there. P0 reaches 90% of C in n1|pop by 0.002 OES only (P0 / C = 0.904).

findings.claim: P0u (the literal P0) is below P0 in the block and object views
findings.check: confounded: P0u trained for 3,000 steps and the conditioned net for 6,000, and both were still improving (block n1: conditioned 0.217 at 3,000 and 0.207 at 6,000; P0u 0.2295 at 3,000)

findings.claim: the state-given gap predicts sigma (rank correlation +0.77 over nine cells); a cheap screen
findings.check: +0.77 reproduced (unadjusted p 0.02; one of 44 correlations; the nine cells are 3 sets of worlds in 3 views). Better evidence, not in the report: over the 24 worlds of a view, the per-world sigma against the per-world gap has a rank correlation of +0.74 (block), +0.47 (object), +0.52 (population), positive in all nine cells. Across views the screen mis-orders: object gaps (0.16-0.24) exceed block gaps (0.13-0.20) while sigma is lower. Use it within one view and predictor family.

findings.claim: rank correlation of sigma with the number of hidden parameters -0.05, with the view dimension -0.50
findings.check: wrong by the tie handling: 0.00 and -0.53 (edits above); no conclusion changes

findings.claim: depth does not cost episodes (ratios 0.2-0.9); the 30x trigger is not met
findings.check: ratios reproduced (0.48, 0.55, 0.65 object; 0.23, 0.89, 0.29 population). The trigger is not met on this evidence, with two caveats: each view has its own net family and its own target (90% of a C at 0.35-0.69), and finding 6 applies to the block and object values.
